Music Nerd · 1424 candidate update · actual before/after

Same questions, candidate update

Compare what listeners actually saw before and after the candidate update. Each of the 17 cards keeps the saved interface output, its citations, and any preceding turn context.

17 known-case checks · 93 accounted calls across these three runs · $0.68964025 combined run actual cost.

Original 11-case report · Six-case extension report

These are known-case regression checks, not held-out cases. The independent review of the after run is shown per case only if locked.

Independent review summary

  • Delivery improved from the five original application errors to displayed responses, without establishing a cause or general reliability.
  • LATASHÁ and Bio Ritmo receive useful bounded answers; Bio Ritmo follow-up advances; Broey reporting time is anchored; Dutchyyy credits surface and its follow-up retains role/unfinished-vocal qualifications.
  • Tom Vek still lacks cross-record sonic comparison despite relevant eligible corpus evidence.
  • Pete introduction/follow-up regress from useful IOI context to rush metadata. 72 Rats first answer has an orphaned Another option, and the follow-up loses a supported first-EP fact bundled with an overclaim.
  • Sound of Fractures remains an honest empty-corpus stop.
  • No answered turn exercised targeted quote-repair feedback: 14 drafts and 14 checkers, one of each per answered turn. F06 completion cannot validate that mechanism.

Mixed known-case evidence, with concrete improvements and retained regressions. Not a general quality pass, held-out confirmation, production reliability claim, or broad issue closure.

Review basis: Reviewer previously reviewed implementation, questions, controls and prior outputs. Parent disclosed some interim outcome concerns before terminal review; this review is independent but not blinded. Fixed-v1 outputs and source traces were opened only after parent reported terminal completion.

What gives Bio Ritmo their sound?

Bio Ritmo's sound is built mostly on New York, Puerto Rican and Fania Records salsa, but they've branched off into their own niche. 1 They pair vintage grooves with experimental synth tones, and cite Stereolab and Brazilian psychedelic music alongside Ray Barretto, Roberto Roena and classic Fania records as influences. 2 Rei Alvarez said the band's mission was original music in the classic salsa style, with experimentation as part of that tradition. 2

Run methods, code pins, and limits

The before side combines the original 11-case fan evaluation and the later six-case extension. The after side uses the same 17 frozen questions and the fixed saved-corpus export; per-artist saved-original counts are checked against both prior availability snapshots. No corpus passage is included in this page.

The runs use the actual AskAboutArtist flow, research client, Web routes, API source selection, and saved navigator. Authentication, persistence, and durable job lifecycle use in-memory harness seams; this does not establish deployed authentication, jobs, or production latency, and no external source collection was performed. The before runs used Node 23 and the candidate-update run used Node 24, so the comparison does not isolate code changes as the cause of any difference.

All 17 questions are known-case regression checks. The earlier answers were already seen during development, so this is not held-out evidence and should not be read as a general quality benchmark. Reports show the actual saved interface output and source links without rewriting answers.

The extension interprets the requested singular name “Sound of Fracture” as the canonical official plural name, Sound of Fractures. That alias interpretation identifies the requested project; it does not prove account ownership. Zero eligible saved originals for Sound of Fractures is a saved-corpus coverage gap, not proof that no public knowledge exists.
